result.reply:
**Low confidence (I can't actually resolve this from what you've pasted) — these two numbers genuinely conflict, and nothing here tells me which one's current or authoritative.**

Two different possible explanations, and I can't rule either in or out from what I have:

1. **Public docs are stale** — someone tightened the internal SLA to 200ms and never pushed the change to the public page, which still shows the old 250ms figure.
2. **Public docs are intentionally looser** — 250ms is a deliberate customer-facing buffer above the real internal target of 200ms, so ops holds itself to a tighter number than what's promised externally. That's a pretty common pattern and wouldn't be a bug at all.

Both are plausible and I have no way to tell which from two flat text snippets — no timestamps, no owner, no changelog.

What would actually let me call this:
- Last-modified date on each page/doc (whichever changed more recently is more likely the "current truth," though even that's not conclusive if the older one was intentional)
- Who owns the public docs page — if it's the same team that sets the SLA, a mismatch is more likely just drift; if it's a separate marketing/docs team, the gap may be deliberate
- Any changelog or PR history on either doc

Without one of those, calling either number "the real one" would be me guessing dressed up as a finding. If you can grab timestamps or ownership on either doc, I can actually run this down instead of flagging it as unresolved.
